objective: Determine how rapidly a large scale fire grows in low-gravity and investigate the low-g flammability limits compared to those obtained in NASA's normal gravity material flammability screening test.
variables_changed: material; thickness; flow direction (igniter position); ignition power; ignition time; planned airflow (DoD Table 1: 20 or 30 cm/s)
sensors: thermocouples (flow, flame/sample and plume temperature); 4 radiometers; CO2 sensor; O2 sensor; pressure sensor; 2 anemometers; 2 cameras; smoke wire
x_notes: n_tests counts tests.csv rows: 9 samples/ignitions, with sample 2-7 split into PMMA and Nomex rows by team decision. year from sensor timestamps (21 Nov 2016); PSI metadata gives investigation dates 09-30-2016 to 04-01-2017; pre-flight paper planned operations for 19 Sep 2016. fuel_type "solid" is a QABAS label (metadata sub-research area: Surface Combustion). O2 range is from the experiment table (derived values); pressure range is measured; airflow range is from the experiment table, measured anemometer means were 19.99 to 25 cm/s. objective and platform/hardware from PSI metadata; sensors from DoD Table 3.
